citation: Aloe, A. M., Shisler, S. M., Norris, B. D., Nickerson, A. B., & Rinker, T. W. (2014). A multivariate meta-analysis of student misbehavior and teacher burnout. Educational Research Review, 12, 30–44.
scope_limitation: 21 independent samples; student misbehavior associated with burnout dimensions. Observational findings do not determine causality.

citation: Maier, S. F., & Seligman, M. E. P. (2016). Learned helplessness at fifty: Insights from neuroscience. Psychological Review, 123(4), 349–367.
scope_limitation: Controllability research; much mechanistic evidence comes from animal experiments. Do not equate occupational stress directly with laboratory conditions.

citation: Bakker, A. B., Demerouti, E., & Sanz-Vergel, A. (2023). Job demands–resources theory: Ten years later. Annual Review of Organizational Psychology and Organizational Behavior, 10, 25–53.
scope_limitation: Job demands and resources, including autonomy and social support, are central to understanding burnout and engagement.

citation: World Health Organization. (2019). Burn-out an occupational phenomenon: International Classification of Diseases.
scope_limitation: Burnout is an occupational phenomenon, not a medical condition; it includes exhaustion, job-related cynicism/distance, and reduced efficacy.

citation: Grandey, A. A., Dickter, D. N., & Sin, H.-P. (2004). The customer is not always right: Customer aggression and emotion regulation of service employees. Journal of Organizational Behavior, 25, 397–418.
scope_limitation: Customer aggression and emotional regulation among service workers; adjacent-sector evidence, not a direct teacher study.
